# Data frame failures

<small>Source: [`R/errors.R`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/r-dataexcept/blob/main/R/errors.R) · Help: `?data_frame_errors`</small>

Errors about the shape of a data frame: a required column that is absent, a
column of the wrong type, and a join whose keys do not line up. All three
inherit from `dataexcept_data_frame_error`, so one handler can catch the
family.

## Usage

```r
missing_column_error(column, dataframe = NULL, parent = NULL, call = NULL)

dtype_mismatch_error(column, expected, found, parent = NULL, call = NULL)

merge_key_error(left_keys, right_keys, parent = NULL, call = NULL)
```

## Arguments

`column`
:   Name of the column.

`dataframe`
:   Optional name of the data frame, for the message.

`parent`
:   The condition that caused this one, or `NULL`.

`call`
:   The call to report, or `NULL`.

`expected`
:   Character vector of acceptable types, such as
    `c("numeric", "integer")`.

`found`
:   The type actually found, typically `class(x)[1]`.

`left_keys`, `right_keys`
:   Character vectors of join keys.

## Value

A condition inheriting from `dataexcept_data_frame_error`.

## Examples

```r
orders <- data.frame(id = 1:3, amount = c("10", "20", "30"))

require_numeric <- function(df, column) {
  if (!column %in% names(df)) {
    stop(missing_column_error(column, dataframe = "orders"))
  }
  if (!is.numeric(df[[column]])) {
    stop(dtype_mismatch_error(column, "numeric", class(df[[column]])[1]))
  }
  invisible(df)
}

tryCatch(
  require_numeric(orders, "amount"),
  dataexcept_data_frame_error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)
```
